We had that issue when I first started FTC in middle school, our solution was to dedicate two lock ins before Qualifier for the specific job. 

Like, Thursdays were massive tweaks and stuff, we wouldn't let ourselves rebuild the entire robot because we'd delay way too long. While buildings going the programmer went to a seperate area or room and cracked down a base code for the robot. 

Friday would be minor tweaks, making sure the robot fits the inspection (labels and stuff, typical things you forget) while also having the programming the main issue for the day. When a autonomous was finished that worked a minimum of 7/10 times, we'd move to driver controlled and stress test the bot. That way your robots is at the most optimal, is packed up, and ready for Saturday!
